[PATH:empirical] Ex-post econometric analysis of the impact of the EU-ECOWAS Economic Partnership Agreement on cocoa exports from Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, 2015-2025 — Directly tests the hypothesis by measuring actual export revenue changes in targeted cash crops after tariff elimination, controlling for confounding factors like global price shocks.

[PATH:theoretical] General equilibrium model of trade liberalization for Sub-Saharan Africa (e.g., GTAP-based simulations) calibrated to coffee, tea, and horticultural supply chains in Ethiopia and Kenya — Provides counterfactual predictions of revenue impacts under tariff elimination scenarios, allowing comparison with observed outcomes and identification of structural conditions (e.g., infrastructure, market access) that may moderate effects.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of free trade agreements and agricultural export performance in Sub-Saharan Africa (World Bank, UNCTAD, or IFPRI working papers, 2015–2025) — Synthesizes existing empirical findings across multiple countries and crops, assessing the consistency of the 15-25% revenue increase claim and highlighting methodological limitations or contextual dependencies.

[PATH:empirical] World Bank's Exporter Dynamics Database and tariff-line trade data for ASEAN and SSA countries (2010-2025) — Provides granular, panel-level trade flow data allowing difference-in-differences estimation of FTA treatment effects on export revenues, controlling for global demand shocks and country-specific trends.

[PATH:literature] UNCTAD's Trade and Development Report (2020-2025 issues) focusing on regional integration effects in developing economies — Offers synthesized case-study evidence and policy analysis specific to Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting heterogeneous outcomes and potential mechanisms (e.g., preference erosion, value chain upgrading).

[PATH:theoretical] Gravity model meta-analysis of FTA impacts on developing country exports (e.g., Baier & Bergstrand, 2007; recent extensions with structural estimation) — Provides a rigorous theoretical framework and empirical consensus estimates, helping to disentangle short-term revenue effects from long-run welfare gains, and identifying conditions under which FTAs may fail to boost export revenues.

[PATH:empirical] ILO labor force surveys and sectoral employment data for Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand (2000-2020) — These surveys provide granular, time-series data on worker reallocation from agriculture and manufacturing into informal services and digital economy sectors, allowing direct testing of the displacement-to-services transition mechanism.

[PATH:empirical] World Bank's Export Diversification and Structural Transformation Database — This database tracks trade liberalization episodes and subsequent shifts in output and employment across tradable and non-tradable sectors, enabling cross-country comparison to isolate the effect of WTO integration on service sector acceleration.

[PATH:theoretical] Rodrik (2016) 'Premature Deindustrialization' in Journal of Economic Growth — This paper provides a theoretical framework predicting that trade-induced displacement in developing economies leads to a shift toward low-productivity services, offering a testable mechanism and benchmark for the hypothesis.

C009.subject: export-oriented free trade policies combined with targeted R&D subsidies
C009.predicate: accelerate the transition from imitative to indigenous innovation in
C009.object: middle-income developing economies within technology sectors
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: export-oriented free trade policies combined with targeted R&D subsidies middle-income developing economies within technology sectors]

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal firm-level panel data from semiconductor and software firms in South Korea (1980s-1990s) and Taiwan (1990s-2000s), tracking R&D spending, patent citations, and export shares — These historical cases exemplify middle-income economies that combined export-oriented policies with targeted R&D subsidies. Panel data can test whether the 30% market share threshold preceded a shift from imitative to indigenous innovation, providing direct causal evidence for the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Comparative case studies of Vietnam and Thailand's technology sectors post-2010, using patent data and innovation surveys to measure indigenous vs. imitative innovation before and after policy implementation — Vietnam and Thailand represent contemporary middle-income developing economies with varying export and R&D subsidy regimes. A controlled comparison can isolate the effect of the policy combination on innovation type, especially given the 10-15 year timeframe specified.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical models of directed technical change with learning-by-exporting and R&D spillovers (e.g., Acemoglu, 2002; Grossman & Helpman, 1991) extended to include market share thresholds — Existing theory suggests export orientation can induce innovation, but the explicit condition of a 30% market share threshold is novel. A formal model can clarify whether such a threshold is necessary or sufficient, and under what conditions the policy accelerates indigenous innovation.

scope.domain: semiconductor manufacturing and software development industries

qualifier.condition: when domestic firms achieve minimum 30% market share in regional exports
